claim: Let \(K\) be Cervone's unique 1133 eight-vertex triangulation of the Klein bottle. For each nonzero class \(\xi\in H^1(K;\mathbf F_2)\), let \(w(\xi)\) be the minimum number of edges in the support of a simplicial one-cocycle representing \(\xi\), and let \(m(\xi)\) be the number of representatives attaining that minimum. Then \(H^1(K;\mathbf F_2)\cong\mathbf F_2^2\), and its three nonzero classes have, in an intrinsic ordering by the cup square \(q(\xi)=\langle\xi\smile\xi,[K]\rangle\), exactly the triples \((w,m,q)=(5,1,1),(6,5,0),(6,3,1)\). The unique weight-five representative is supported on the five edges \(BC,BG,CE,DE,DG\). Every minimizing support for all three nonzero classes is a single simple cycle in the dual graph of the triangulation.

integrity.claim_scope: complete nonzero mod-two one-cosystolic profile of the 1133 eight-vertex Klein-bottle triangulation
integrity.proof_core: exact cochain linear algebra, exhaustive cocycle-coset enumeration, cup-square evaluation, and dual-cycle connectivity checks
integrity.unproved_limits: No statement is made for integral coefficients, subdivisions, other minimal Klein-bottle triangulations, or an infinite family.

scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns only Cervone's fixed 1133 eight-vertex triangulation and coefficients in \(\mathbf F_2\).
The classwise support minima and multiplicities are proved by exhaustive enumeration of all \(512\) cocycles after exact rank reduction; no infinite-family claim is made.
An obscure or unindexed historical computation under dual-cycle or coding terminology remains a residual literature risk.
title: The asymmetrical eight-vertex Klein bottle has mod-two cosystolic profile \(5,6,6\)
